_directive: machine-facing parameterized source-quality rubric; deterministic scoring over a source object.
purpose: Score a single source object on a 0..1 quality scale combining CRAAP-style dimensions (authority, recency, relevance), plus a corroboration credit and an independence guard. Used by acquisition_ledger.py score-source and as advisory input when deciding evidence_label legality.

authority.description: Expertise/credentials/standing of the source (CRAAP Authority). Read directly from source.authority.

recency.description: Currency of the source for the topic's volatility (CRAAP Currency). Read directly from source.recency.

relevance.description: Topical fit to the competency question (CRAAP Relevance). Read directly from source.relevance.

independence.description: Independence credit. When scoring a source IN CONTEXT of a ledger entry, a source sharing its independence_group with another source on the same CQ is dependent corroboration and earns 0.0 here; a source in a singleton independence_group earns 1.0. When scored standalone (no context), defaults to 1.0.

corroboration.description: Corroboration credit = (count of DISTINCT independence_groups on the same CQ minus 1), clamped to [0,1]. Standalone scoring (no context) yields 0.0 (a lone source cannot be corroborated).

notes: This rubric scores SOURCE quality (an admissibility/weighting signal). It does NOT by itself set a claim's evidence_label.
evidence_label legality is enforced separately in acquisition_ledger.py validate: a 'high' label needs >=2 sources in DISTINCT independence_groups; 'moderate' needs >=1 source.
independence mirrors argue's rule: items sharing a common upstream source are collapsed before counting corroboration.
